description: Variable-mass launch vehicles as 3D bond graphs: a V-2 vertical shot and the Saturn V AS-506 ascent to parking orbit. Checks against an independent scipy integration (tight), Tsiolkovsky (exact, in vacuum) and published data (V-2: Wikipedia; Saturn V: the AS-506 flight evaluation report MPR-SAT-FE-69-9), with the tolerances and fitted quantities named in each note.

checks.note: no derivative causality, no algebraic loop warning, no event storm and no solver failure
burnout speed of the scipy reference (design/reference.py, the same equations integrated as a planar point mass with DOP853)
burnout altitude, scipy reference
apogee of the scipy reference
time of apogee (the flight-path angle turns from +90 to -90 deg), scipy reference on a 0.1 s output grid
Mach 1, scipy reference
max Q on the way up, scipy reference (0.1 s grid: the peak is sampled, hence 2e-3)
mass at burnout: m0 - mdot t_burn = 4505 kg (the flow lag starts the decay only at t_burn)
PUBLISHED: burnout speed 'about 5,000 ft/s (1,500 m/s)' (Wikipedia, V-2 sounding rocket). Different payloads and loads flew; the model gives 1422 m/s (5 % low). Loose tolerance 10 %.

PUBLISHED: White Sands design profile 'about 100 miles (160 km) high' (Wikipedia, V-2 sounding rocket). The model reaches 141.7 km (11 % low: the drag table and the propellant load are estimates). Loose tolerance 15 %.
PUBLISHED: never above the 206 km maximum for a vertical launch (Wikipedia, V-2 rocket)

TSIOLKOVSKY: without gravity, drag and atmosphere the speed is c_vac ln(m0/mf) = 2312.14 m/s * ln(12500/4464.41) (mf includes the lagged thrust decay mdot tau). Exact: tests the variable-mass bond graph (MI + outflow MR).
ideal velocity gain = Tsiolkovsky in vacuum
final mass m0 - mdot (t_burn + tau (1 - exp(-15/tau)))
no derivative causality, no algebraic loop warning, no event storm and no solver failure
